correctness.rationale: The complete allocation must be four cross-category pairs because there are eight goods and total rank quota two for each agent; independently enumerating unordered matchings of three categories of sizes 3,3,2 yields exactly 36, then 4! ordered placements yield exactly 864 allocations. For binary approval counts 0,1,2, EF1 between i and j fails exactly if own approved count is zero and the other pair has count two; prescribed-order nonenvy requires own count >= each later pair count. Inspected C++ bitset exhaustive coverage algorithm computes all later-agent admissibility masks on 864 allocations for all 256 valuations each, intersects over all 256^3=16,777,216 triples, and unions their 256-bit admissible first-agent masks; every triple covers all 256 masks. The actual compiled C++17 source reported allocations=864, checked triples=16777216, binary preference profiles=4294967296, failed triples=0. Independent literal EF1 checking tested 69,536 further valuation profiles and verified 36 pairings, 864 allocations. For arbitrary nonnegative two-level singleton values a_i and a_i+b_i, equal two-good bundle size preserves ordered comparisons by affine transformation, and after EF1 removal the current-own advantage adds +a_i>=0. Agent relabelling yields every prescribed order. This is an exhaustive finite proof of all 2^32 binary preference profiles, not a sample or infinite search.
residual_risks: Matroid is exactly the 8-good (3,3,2) three-category rank-two laminar key and there are exactly four agents; only heterogeneous nonnegative two-level additive valuations.
Does not establish existence for arbitrary additive values, 12-good key, EFX or efficiency, and does not eliminate priority uncertainty about unindexed finite exhaustive work.
